audio_caption: The clip begins with a promotional announcement by a male speaker, advertising a website for purchasing Madden Ultimate Team coins and providing a discount code. This shifts into a heavy rock style musical passage, dominated by a fast guitar riff and strong drum beat, accompanied by a male shouting. A male voice then says, "Hello," then the prior promo speaker can be heard saying "It says good morning, MMG", who continues to describe playing a game. He then mentions making coffee for "JMO," followed by coffee grinding sounds. A second male voice exclaims "Pubes." Both men speak in more hushed tones, when the second male voice shouts "Shut the hell up," followed by the first male's offer, "I bring you, Cafesi." The second man repeats "You bring me cafesi." The first man repeats "I do. What do you want?" Both male voices repeat "What do you want?" followed by a dog barking and one of the men saying, "No."

The audio clip begins with a male speaker expressing confidence that the Lions will win, followed by sounds of a dog happily barking. The same male speaker then makes a statement about a football coach being the worst ever. A female voice responds with sarcasm, stating that the coach won't be fired due to the existence of another coach. The male speaker then proposes an exaggerated question about a different coach potentially needing imprisonment. This is followed by sounds of laughter.

The clip starts with a male speaker discussing his breakfast plans, mentioning coffee and considering options. Background sounds suggest he's cooking, with sizzling noises and the sounds of a toaster. He describes making toast, eggs, ham, and turkey. A brief, loud burst of sound, almost like a sudden flare-up, cuts through. There's more cooking sound, followed by the speaker commenting on the food's appearance. Another male voice interjects, followed by more sounds of food preparation. Finally, a male sports announcer discusses a sports game.

The audio clip starts with a male speaker discussing football and fantasy leagues, suggesting it's time to "bench Baker Mayfield" after a bad play and mentioning taking his "fantasy team and throwing it in the trashcan," expressing frustration and dissatisfaction. He then introduces the topic of showing his fantasy team, characterizing it as "one of the saddest things you'll ever see." He describes the league setup and how his initial picks were missed, after which "everything else just went to shit so fast."

The audio clip starts with a male speaker humorously listing players out of the football league due to injury, expressing disbelief at his current starting running backs. He sounds disheartened while mentioning key injuries, particularly Dak Prescott's absence, and his misfortunes in team selection. A comedic tone follows as he evaluates his team's prospects, admitting it’s embarrassing, but ending by stating that his team isn't playing bad, noting his chance of winning. Then the speaker laughs and states “it’s not funny bro, this is my life.” The conversation ends with a comment about always saying next year will be his year.

The audio clip begins with speech; a male speaker says "that's cold blooded", followed by another male speaker stating "let's go operator. Fifty bomb. Right down the schmiddle. Easy money." He then says "I miss Dak Prescott". Another male speaker mentions "imagine losing to a team that doesn't have a mascot." and suggests "couldn't be me Dallas Cowboys." The next speaker declares "This man is convinced that DeAndre Swift is the next Alvin Kamara" repeating "yes" and calling someone "Bad Alvin Kamara right there". Following this, the same speaker mentions the phrase "next Kamara." After this, a speaker shouts "Kamara." The speaker then says "10 to 14 I predicted on Twitter would be 31 to 21 Lions. And we're technically on good pace for that, cause we have our one field goal already. Lots going on right now.

The audio clip begins with a male speaker excitedly announcing a field goal by Prater, remarking on the game score and giving his predictions about the outcome. He shifts to another game, mentioning scores and player performances, expressing personal interest and opinions. He reflects humorously on the possibility of losing to a team whose starting quarterback is Kyle Allen. There is a male speaker reflecting on his game.

The audio clip starts with two male voices discussing a football game, expressing frustration as one says, "don't, just throw a pick," and "it's over if they get this." An interception occurs, prompting an exasperated "he fucking got it." The speakers express dismay over the Atlanta Falcons' performance and an intercepted pass with one asking "Why would you throw that?" They discuss how he "throw the check down" and "kick a field goal" but then say he just "threw the triple coverage." The discussion continues, critiquing the play calling. There is a pause, then one asks, "wait, did you score?" This leads to excited laughter as he exclaims, "we can actually win." A bit of music in a lighthearted mood plays in the background. Then, the speaker says, "He crossed the line." He then exclaims, "oh my god." They then excitedly state, "All right, they got the two point."

The clip opens with excited commentary on a football game, remarking that "Stafford's built for this". The excited male speaker observes the game's progress, mentioning details like a "fourth and inches" play, followed by a touchdown. There is an observation that the current score mirrors a previous game. A burst of frustration is expressed with someone shouting "spike it! Spike the goddamn ball!". The speaker questions the reason for a flag, mentioning a possible penalty for delaying the spike, then confirms a catch with elation. A prediction is made about a successful season. The speaker then expresses concern about the Steelers potentially being undefeated. The commentary continues, noting timeouts and plays, including the speaker warning not to "DPI that" and praising a catch. The speaker becomes anxious about a potential ten-second run-down.

The audio clip begins with an outburst from a male speaker, expressing frustration over perceived game losses due to a "10-second rundown rule," which he describes as "bullshit." He conveys intense emotion and annoyance. The speaker then transitions to a softer tone, predicting that the game is "about to be OT." The clip concludes with sounds from a sporting event, including crowd noises.

The clip begins with a male voice exclaiming in distress. Following this is a short burst of what sounds like upbeat, casual music. Then a second male voice speaks, describing a sports bet and its outcome, specifically mentioning "steelers to win and the over". The clip concludes with a brief, indistinct sound effect.

The audio clip starts with a male speaker excitedly yelling "Oh!" followed by "Oh, juicy tree!" and expressing disbelief with "Oh my God, we could do it." He then questions, in a challenging tone, the presented win probability, saying "You're giving me a 4% chance to catch this ball?", concluding "You're out of your mind next-gen stats, this s**t's over." This is followed by encouragement with "Let's go baby, come on baby, come on baby," as cheering sounds enter the background. There is a sound resembling running footsteps and another yell. Jubilant yells are repeated: "Let's go! Let's go!" interspersed with an indistinguishable phrase and "F**king tunnel!" More cheering is heard before he yells "Get sh**t out, oh, we gotta hit the PAT", referring to a point-after attempt in football, and exclaims "Let's f**king go!" The clip concludes with, in an angry tone, "4% my d**k and balls, next-gen stats!" and an indistinguishable yell.

The audio clip features initially excited male speech exclaiming, "Oh my god! He f***ing right before us!" This exclamation shifts to a tone of disbelief mixed with humor, followed by a more measured observation of "4% my d*** and balls. Let's go." Then, the tone shifts to critical commentary, "sunk the game," expressing disappointment in a player's actions. In the background, a muffled sound accompanies the male speech. Then, there's a further male voice exclaiming, "And the ball just caught light!" expressing shock or surprise.

The clip starts with a male voice exclaiming "Holy sh*t, what is going on?", expressing shock. There's a quick succession of enthusiastic, excited male voices mentioning sports players and football terms like "People's Jones," "Lions," "PAT," and "off-sides," indicating they are watching a game. Sounds of electronic music or beats begin subtly, suggesting an intensifying atmosphere. As the game commentary persists with mentions of penalties and strategic play calls, the music becomes more pronounced, building anticipation. A joyous shout of "Yes!" bursts out, coupled with celebratory laughter and a declaration of "12 and 4, it's coming, baby!", followed by a sound like a celebratory yell. The music surges alongside a man's awed exclamation of "Holy Sh*t, boys!" and "Let's go!" before the clip concludes with amused laughter.

The clip begins with an enthusiastic male speaker expressing excitement, saying, "Oh my god, I'm so happy this is the week I started filming this uh, this Sunday thing. Holy shit." The speaker then mentions several football players by name ("Stafford goated, Hockenson goated") and ends with saying, "disgrace to my name." Then, the same speaker transitions to a closing statement, mentioning watching a Seahawks Cardinals game.

The audio clip begins with a male speaker expressing excitement ("Oh my god"). He hopes the audience saw "the best football game" he has seen in a while. The speaker expresses disappointment that he was unable to record his reaction for the entire game, promising to improve in future episodes, thanking viewers for watching, and signing off with "Peace." Afterward, electronic instrumental music starts playing, featuring a laid-back mood and prominent synth sounds.
